title_ar: حكم اشتراط الزوجة على زوجها ألا سابقة عليها ولا لاحقة لها || فتاوى الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو
title_en: The Ruling on a Wife Stipulating to Her Husband That There Be No Wife Before Her and None After Her || Fatwas of Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew
body_ar:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم، وصلي الله وسلم على المبعوث رحمة للعالمين سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وصحبه ومن تبعهم بإحسان إلى يوم الدين، وبعد فقد كلفني أحد المشايخ المقيمين في البادية بطرح استشكال على فضيلتكم يتعلق بالشرط المعروف في أغلب عقود الزواج بقطرنا، والمتعلق باشتراط المرأة في صلب العقد ( أن لا سابقة لها، ولا لاحقة عليها، وإلا فأمرها بيدها، أو بيد وليها إن كان) وقبول الزوج الصريح للشرط ورضاه هل هو داخل في دائرة التخيير، ويترتب عليه حق الزوجة في أن تختار التحلل من العصمة أوالبقاء على ذمة الزوج إذا هو أخل بالشرط بأن تزوج عليها، أوظهر أن على ذمته أخرى سابقة لها؟، أم أن الشرط باطل أصلا من أساسه، وتضمينه العقد لا يغير من حق الزوج في التعدد شيئا، ولا يترتب على إخلاله به أي أثر يدعم اعتراض الزوجة على ممارسة زوجها حقه في ماشرع الله له؟.

---- الجواب -----

و عليكم السلام و رحمة الله و بركاته
المسألة محل خلاف بين أهل العلم و الراجح عندي فيها أن هذا الشرط باطل لا يترتب عليه أي شيء لما ثبت في الصحيحين عَنْ عَائِشَةَ قَالَتْ: جَاءَتْنِي بَرِيرَةُ فَقَالَتْ : كَاتَبْتُ أَهْلِي عَلَى تِسْعِ أَوَاقٍ، فِي كُلِّ عَامٍ أُوقِيَّةٌ، فَأَعِينِينِي، فَقَالَتْ: إِنْ أَحَبُّوا أَنْ أَعُدَّهَا لَهُمْ وَيَكُونَ وَلَاؤُكِ لِي فَعَلْتُ. فَذَهَبَتْ بَرِيرَةُ إِلَى أَهْلِهَا، فَقَالَتْ لَهُمْ فَأَبَوْا عَلَيْهَا، فَجَاءَتْ مِنْ عِنْدِهِمْ وَرَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ جَالِسٌ، فَقَالَتْ : إِنِّي قَدْ عَرَضْتُ ذَلِكِ عَلَيْهِمْ فَأَبَوْا، إِلَّا أَنْ يَكُونَ الْوَلَاءُ لَهُمْ. فَسَمِعَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، فَأَخْبَرَتْ عَائِشَةُ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فَقَالَ: " خُذِيهَا وَاشْتَرِطِي لَهُمُ الْوَلَاءَ ؛ فَإِنَّمَا الْوَلَاءُ لِمَنْ أَعْتَقَ ". فَفَعَلَتْ عَائِشَةُ، ثُمَّ قَامَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فِي النَّاسِ، فَحَمِدَ اللَّهَ وَأَثْنَى عَلَيْهِ، ثُمَّ قَالَ : " مَا بَالُ رِجَالٍ يَشْتَرِطُونَ شُرُوطًا لَيْسَتْ فِي كِتَابِ اللَّهِ ؟ مَا كَانَ مِنْ شَرْطٍ لَيْسَ فِي كِتَابِ اللَّهِ فَهُوَ بَاطِلٌ، وَإِنْ كَانَ مِائَةَ شَرْطٍ، قَضَاءُ اللَّهِ أَحَقُّ، وَشَرْطُ اللَّهِ أَوْثَقُ، وَإِنَّمَا الْوَلَاءُ لِمَنْ أَعْتَقَ ". و لقوله صلى الله عليه و سلم الصُّلْحُ جَائِزٌ بَيْنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ إِلَّا صُلْحًا حَرَّمَ حَلَالًا، أَوْ أَحَلَّ حَرَامًا، وَالْمُسْلِمُونَ عَلَى شُرُوطِهِمْ، إِلَّا شَرْطًا حَرَّمَ حَلَالًا، أَوْ أَحَلَّ حَرَامًا " أخرجه الترمذي بإسناد صحيح
و قد سئل عمر رضي الله عنه عن هذا الشرط فقال سبق شرط الله شرطها. و قد عقد مالك في الموطإ بابا لهذا و هو باب ما لا يجوز من الشروط في النكاح و فيه قَالَ مَالِكٌ : فَالْأَمْرُ عِنْدَنَا، أَنَّهُ إِذَا اشْتَرَطَ الرَّجُلُ لِلْمَرْأَةِ، وَإِنْ كَانَ ذَلِكَ عِنْدَ عُقْدَةِ النِّكَاحِ : أَنْ لَا أَنْكِحَ عَلَيْكِ، وَلَا أَتَسَرَّرَ. إِنَّ ذَلِكَ لَيْسَ بِشَيْءٍ، إِلَّا أَنْ يَكُونَ فِي ذَلِكَ يَمِينٌ بِطَلَاقٍ، أَوْ عِتَاقَةٍ، فَيَجِبُ ذَلِكَ عَلَيْهِ وَيَلْزَمُهُ.
و الله يوفقنا و إياكم لكل خير
body_en:
In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Mercy-Giving. May God bless and grant peace to the one sent as a mercy to the worlds, our master Muhammad, and to his family and his Companions and those who follow them in excellence until the Day of Judgement. To proceed: one of the sheikhs living out in the countryside has charged me with putting a difficulty to Your Eminence concerning the condition well known in most marriage contracts in our country, namely the woman's stipulating in the body of the contract (that there be no wife before her and none after her, and that otherwise her affair is in her own hand, or in the hand of her guardian if she has one), together with the husband's express acceptance of the condition and his consent to it. Does it fall within the scope of the option to divorce (takhyīr), so that there follows from it the wife's right to choose release from the marriage bond (ʿiṣmah) or remaining in her husband's charge, if he breaches the condition by marrying another alongside her, or it emerges that he already has another wife in his charge from before her? Or is the condition void from its very foundation, so that writing it into the contract changes nothing of the husband's right to plural marriage, and no effect follows from his breaching it that would support the wife's objection to her husband exercising his right in what God has legislated for him?

---- The Answer -----

And upon you be peace, and the mercy of God and His blessings.
The question is one on which the people of knowledge disagree, and the preponderant view in my judgement is that this condition is void (bāṭil) and that nothing follows from it, because of what is established in the two Ṣaḥīḥs from Aisha, who said: Barira came to me and said: I have contracted with my owners for my emancipation for nine ūqiyyahs, one ūqiyyah each year; so help me. [Aisha] said: If they are willing that I count it out for them and that your right of patronage (walāʾ) be mine, I will do it. So Barira went to her owners and said that to them, and they refused it to her; and she came back from them while the Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace, was sitting, and she said: I have put that to them and they refused, except that the right of patronage be theirs. The Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, heard, and Aisha informed the Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: "Take her, and stipulate the right of patronage for them; for the right of patronage belongs only to the one who sets free." So Aisha did so. Then the Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace, rose among the people, praised God and extolled Him, then said: "What is the matter with men who stipulate conditions that are not in the Book of God? Whatever condition is not in the Book of God is void, even if it be a hundred conditions. God's decree (qaḍāʾ) has the better right, and God's condition is the firmer; and the right of patronage belongs only to the one who sets free." And because of his saying, God bless him and grant him peace: Reconciliation is permissible between Muslims, except a reconciliation that forbids what is lawful or makes lawful what is forbidden; and the Muslims are held to their conditions, except a condition that forbids what is lawful or makes lawful what is forbidden" — narrated by al-Tirmidhi with a sound chain.
Umar, may God be pleased with him, was asked about this condition and said: God's condition takes precedence over her condition. And Malik set aside a chapter for this in the Muwatta, namely the chapter on what is not permissible among the conditions in marriage, and in it: Malik said: The position with us is that if a man stipulates to a woman, even if that be at the tying of the marriage contract, that "I shall not marry another alongside you, and I shall not take a concubine" — that is nothing, unless there be in it an oath by divorce or by manumission, in which case it becomes obligatory upon him and binding on him.
And God grant us and you every good.

flags.arabic: و الراجح عندي فيها أن هذا الشرط باطل
flags.context: the Sheikh's own position, given after he notes the disagreement
options: the preponderant view in my judgement is that this condition is void (bāṭil)
what I consider preponderant is that this condition is void
in my view the stronger position is that this condition is invalid
flags.note: This is the ruling of the fatwa and the sentence on which everything turns, so it is flagged for a reviewer's eye rather than because it is doubtful. عندي is 'in my judgement' and must not be dropped: he is stating his own preponderant view on a question he has just said the scholars disagree about, not reporting a consensus. bāṭil is rendered by the glossary's fixed 'void', which concerns the condition's legal effect and not its sinfulness: the Sheikh is saying the stipulation produces no effect, not that making it is a sin.

flags.context: the Barira hadith, quoted as the evidence
options: the right of inheritance from a freed slave
flags.note: walāʾ is not in the glossary. It is the tie between a freed slave and the person who freed them, carrying rights of inheritance and of legal protection. 'Patronage' is the established English rendering. Option 2 states only one of its effects. Needed as a glossary addition.

flags.context: inside the Prophet's address in the Barira hadith
options: God's decree (qaḍāʾ) has the better right
God's ordinance has the prior claim
flags.note: Style guide section 13 lists qaḍāʾ as a pending glossary addition in its theological sense, distinct from the two senses the glossary already carries ('judicial ruling' and making up a missed act of worship). Neither existing sense fits here: this is God's decree as against a human stipulation. Flagged rather than assumed.

flags.arabic: أن لا أنكح عليك، ولا أتسرر
flags.context: the words of the stipulation in the passage quoted from Malik's Muwatta
options: I shall not marry another alongside you, and I shall not take a concubine
I shall not take another wife, nor a concubine
I shall neither marry again nor keep a slave-concubine
flags.note: tasarrur is taking a slave-concubine. It is quoted here inside an eighth-century text that the Sheikh cites for a different point (that such stipulations produce no effect), and it is not a term the fatwa itself uses of the present day. It has been translated plainly rather than paraphrased away, and flagged, because a euphemism here would be a silent alteration of a quoted classical source.

translator_notes: This record is a complete fatwa: the question is set out in full, the Sheikh gives his own preponderant view, and he then gives his evidence. It is not an excerpt and does not stop before the ruling.
The questioner poses the two possibilities as alternatives and the Sheikh chooses the second. Nothing has been added to the first possibility, which he does not argue for.

The hadith attributions are preserved exactly as the Sheikh gives them: 'what is established in the two Ṣaḥīḥs' for the Barira report, and 'narrated by al-Tirmidhi with a sound chain' for the report on reconciliation. No grading has been added and none dropped.

The source's closing quotation mark on the al-Tirmidhi hadith has no opening partner in the Arabic; the English reproduces the text as served rather than repairing the punctuation (style guide section 11).

أمرها بيدها is the Maliki device by which the wife is given power to dissolve the marriage herself; rendered literally as 'her affair is in her own hand' because the Sheikh treats the phrase as the wording of the contract, not as a technical label.
الموطإ is spelt with a final hamza on the line in the source; preserved in body_ar, rendered 'the Muwatta' in body_en.
editorial_review_reasons: The fatwa holds void a condition, standard in Mauritanian marriage contracts, by which a wife stipulates that her husband take no other wife, and states that including it changes nothing of his right to plural marriage. Published in English this is a ruling on polygamy and on the enforceability of a marriage-contract term; in jurisdictions where polygamous marriage is unlawful and where marriage contracts are enforceable instruments, presenting it without context risks being read as advice that such a term may be disregarded. Translated faithfully and neither softened nor strengthened.

The passage quoted from Malik's Muwatta contains a stipulation about taking a slave-concubine. It is a quotation from a classical source about an institution that no longer exists, and it is reproduced rather than paraphrased so that the Sheikh's evidence is visible; in English, out of context, it is liable to be read as a contemporary position.
